description: This pie chart illustrates the distribution of emotion categories within the IEMOCAP dataset, as referenced in a study on speaker anonymization. The chart is divided into six distinct slices, each representing a different emotional state. The largest segment is labeled "Frustration," colored light blue, and accounts for 25.1% of the distribution. This is followed by "Neutral" in purple at 23.1%, "Anger" in yellow at 14.9%, "Sadness" in orange at 14.7%, "Excitement" in red at 14.1%, and finally "Happiness" in medium blue, which is the smallest slice at 8.1%. Percentage values are displayed directly inside each corresponding slice, while the category text labels are positioned just outside the perimeter of the chart adjacent to their respective segments. The chart does not include a separate legend, nor are any of the slices visually emphasized through explosion or offset. Visually, while the top two largest slices occupy the upper half of the chart, the segments do not follow a strict descending or ascending size order around the entire circumference.
caption_used: The pie chart illustrates the distribution of emotion categories in the IEMOCAP dataset, with percentages displayed relative to the number of utterances. Frustration is the largest category, accounting for approximately 25.1% of the data, followed by Neutral at 23.1%. Anger and Sadness are nearly equal, with Anger slightly higher at 15.9% and Sadness at 14.7%. Excitement and Happiness are the smallest categories, with Happiness at 10.1% and Excitement at 14.1%. Notably, the data suggests a consistent decline in positive emotions (Excitement and Happiness) compared to negative ones (Frustration, Anger, and Sadness). The chart provides a clear visual representation of the emotional distribution, with labels positioned outside each slice for clarity.
